targetDeployment.identityProofMethod: Three independent signals agree: (1) NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL host, (2) CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY's own non-secret prefix (text before the '|' separator, which Convex deploy keys self-declare as '<env>:<deployment-name>'), (3) a live authenticated query using this exact key succeeded (Convex deploy keys are cryptographically bound to one specific deployment, so a mismatched key would fail auth outright rather than silently reading a different deployment).

crawlEntryPoint.whyNoResume: This checkout retained crash-recovery state (crawler_state.json, crawl_ledger.sqlite3, dlq.jsonl) from the ORIGINAL interrupted 2026-08-02 run that built the historical ~992-document corpus on a DIFFERENT (now-superseded) Convex deployment, before the user created this new rugged-bird-156 deployment on another Google account. Default --resume behavior would silently treat this as continuing that old, different-deployment run (crawling only its ~931 leftover queued URLs) rather than a genuine from-scratch crawl of the live site into the new empty database. --no-resume generates a fresh runId, verified via source inspection (scripts/crawler.py:4893-4898) to leave the old state file's content backed up (see stateFilesBackup below) before it gets overwritten by this run's own periodic saves, and the SQLite ledger (scripts/uet_crawler/crawl_ledger.py:182-201) is properly scoped by a (run_id, url) composite primary key so old rows cannot silently bias or skip URLs for the new run_id.
crawlEntryPoint.stateFilesBackup: Pre-existing crawler_state.json, crawl_ledger.sqlite3, dlq.jsonl, crawl_coverage.json, crawl_coverage.csv copied (not moved) to the session scratchpad before this run started, so the historical 2026-08-02 run's evidence is preserved regardless of what this new run does to the same-named files in the project root.
